case_studies.title: WeClawArena: An Auditable Sandbox and Benchmark for Cross-User Agents Collaboration and Security in Human-Centered Agent Networks
case_studies.abstract: Recent advances in persistent personal-agent frameworks are making human-centered agent networks realistic deployment targets: each user can be served by an AI agent that acts on the user's behalf, maintains state, and communicates with other agents through social and task relations. In these networks, everyday tool use becomes multi-party owned-agent collaboration over personal workspaces, where files, records, tools, and policies are not directly visible across owners. Existing agent benchmarks study tool use and collaboration, but they do not provide an end-to-end sandbox for verifiable cro
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of securing cross-user agent collaboration in human-centered agent networks by building a sandbox called WeClawArena. The result is a benchmark for testing the security of these networks. This doesn't directly affect cloud infrastructure management work!

For the same SpMM on the same matrix, cuSPARSE exhibits a 350x performance gap between CSR and Blocked-ELL. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of slow GPU performance in sparse matrix operations by creating a system called SparseDitto that customizes GPU kernels for different sparsity patterns. SparseDitto achieves better performance by adapting its representation, execution strategy, and hardware mapping to each workload. The result is improved GPU performance for various sparse matrix operations.

case_studies.title: CURATE: Leveraging LLM Agents to Compose, Catalog, and Deploy Reproducible Workflows
case_studies.abstract: Agentic code generation has shown promise in automating and accelerating software development by utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate, test, and deploy code. For engineers and scientists, such systems have the potential to accelerate the development of applied and scientific workflows while reducing barriers to entry in domains that have yet to fully realize their benefits. However, a key gap remains: existing coding agents primarily focus on code generation and do not address the entire workflow lifecycle, including deployment and sharing. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of automating the entire workflow lifecycle, including deployment and sharing, by building a system called CURATE that uses Large Language Models to compose, catalog, and deploy reproducible workflows. The result is a system that accelerates software development and reduces barriers to entry in various domains. This research aims to help engineers and scientists develop and share workflows more efficiently.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure for scientific workflows or software development, here is what to do: review your current workflow deployment process, consider integrating CURATE to automate and accelerate workflow composition and deployment, and evaluate the potential benefits of using Large Language Models in your workflow lifecycle.

case_studies.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) continues to evolve and mature, recent AI practices have moved beyond large language models (LLMs) and text or image generation tasks, increasingly integrating tools, agents, and harnesses to solve real business and industrial problems. However, the power of AI is not verified under these real-world complex systems for various reasons, considering reliability, feasibility, resilience, and responsibility requirements in real commercial and industrial operations. case_studies.summary: This research aims to solve the problem of unreliable AI systems in complex real-world environments by introducing Enactive Artificial Intelligence, a decision-centric architecture. The authors built a conceptual framework that integrates tools and agents to improve reliability and resilience. The result is a more robust AI system for commercial and industrial operations.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI-powered systems, here is what to do: review your current architecture for reliability and resilience gaps, assess the feasibility of integrating Enactive AI principles, and evaluate the potential benefits for your organization's complex systems. case_studies.title: RAC: Reference-Aware Activation Compression for Communication-Efficient Split LLM Inference
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents repeatedly process long, privacy-sensitive contexts, while cloud-only deployment exposes user data beyond the trusted endpoint and fully local deployment often requires costly hardware. Split inference offers a middle ground by executing the model head, tail, and tools locally and the middle layers in the cloud, but its local-cloud-local path transfers boundary hidden states at every invocation and creates a critical communication bottleneck. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of communication bottlenecks in split inference for large language models by building a reference-aware codec. The result is a more efficient way to transfer data between local and cloud environments. This could impact cloud infrastructure management for organisations using large language models.

case_studies.title: Chained Recursive Language Models for Multi-Iteration Reasoning
case_studies.abstract: Long context reasoning in large language models (LLMs) is usually constrained by the fact that a single inference trajectory has to simultaneously explore the context, store intermediate state, verify evidence, and produce the final answer. This becomes particularly difficult in tasks that require extraction, counting, ordering, or multi-hop reasoning, where an early mistake can propagate until the final response. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of long context reasoning in large language models by building a new architecture called Chained Recursive Language Models, which allows for repeated calls to the same model to improve accuracy. The result is a more effective way to handle complex tasks like extraction and multi-hop reasoning. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Item Response Theory for AI Safety
case_studies.abstract: Language models differ in how safely they behave and these differences are measured by safety benchmarks. But aggregated benchmark scores are hard to trust and interpret, because benchmarks duplicate one another, correlate heavily, and models may sandbag when they detect evaluation. To address these issues, we draw on Item Response Theory (IRT), a statistical toolkit for measuring these latents from performance on items with inferred psychometric properties. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of trusting and interpreting aggregated safety benchmark scores for language models by using Item Response Theory to measure their safety. The researchers built a statistical model to analyze the performance of 192 language models across eight safety benchmarks. The result provides a more reliable way to evaluate the safety of language models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that deploys language models, here is what to do: review your current safety benchmarking process, consider incorporating Item Response Theory to improve evaluation reliability, and reassess the trustworthiness of your models' safety scores.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper addresses a known issue in LLM safety evaluation, but its relevance to IT infrastructure and potential impact are limited. While IRT modeling is applied to LLMs, the focus is on psychometric analysis rather than deployment or operational impact.

case_studies.abstract: Interdisciplinary research collaboration is crucial for scientific innovation, but it remains difficult to initiate in practice. Existing collaborator discovery approaches are often constrained by disciplinary boundaries and static researcher profiles that do not reflect the specific context of a new collaboration goal. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of initiating interdisciplinary research collaborations by building a visual analytics system called DeepConnect. The system uses large language models to help researchers find suitable collaborators and establish common goals. The result is a more effective way for researchers to work together across different disciplines.

case_studies.title: DASyR-LLM: Domain-Aware Symbolic Regression with LLMs for Kinetic Model Discovery
case_studies.abstract: Kinetic model discovery is a central challenge in chemical engineering, as accurate rate expressions are essential for understanding and controlling chemical and biological processes. Symbolic regression (SR) has emerged as a powerful data-driven approach for identifying interpretable kinetic models, but usually operates without domain knowledge, often exploring physicochemically implausible models. Large language models (LLMs) offer a promising avenue for injecting domain expertise into this search. Here, we introduce an LLM-guided SR framework, embedding an LLM module within an iterative SR
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of kinetic model discovery in chemical engineering by building a framework that combines symbolic regression with large language models, resulting in more accurate and interpretable models. The framework, called DASyR-LLM, embeds an LLM module within an iterative symbolic regression process. This research is not directly relevant to IT work.

case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel combination of symbolic regression and LLMs may intrigue some IT engineers, but lacks immediate practical application for IT infrastructure. case_studies.title: Toward Skill-Native LLMs: Skill Entropy for Benchmarking and Training Long-Horizon Reasoning
case_studies.abstract: Long-horizon reasoning in recent LLMs demands that the model switch between distinct skills inside a reasoning chain, such as first doing a math derivation, then using the result to plan a schedule. We call such problems cross-skill long-horizon tasks: multi-step tasks whose steps require different reasoning skills and depend on earlier outputs. Existing benchmarks often evaluate individual skills, lacking a principled way to measure how well a model switches between skills. We address this gap from both the evaluation and training sides. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating and training long-horizon reasoning in large language models, where the model needs to switch between different skills. The authors built a measure called Skill Entropy to benchmark and train these models. The result is a more effective way to evaluate and improve the performance of large language models in complex tasks.

case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper focuses on improving LLMs, but relevance to everyday IT work is limited. Novelty is moderate, but not particularly surprising. Value lies in potentially improved LLMs which may require significant retraining and infrastructure changes.

case_studies.title: Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming
case_studies.abstract: Prompt injection poses significant security risks to LLM agents. Efficient and effective red-teaming is therefore critical, both for evaluating these risks and for collecting training data to improve defenses. Existing state-of-the-art prompt injection red-teaming methods primarily rely on reinforcement learning (RL), producing attacker models that often generalize poorly to new target LLMs. In this work, we develop PIMiner, an agentic system for prompt injection red-teaming. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of prompt injection security risks in large language models by building a system called PIMiner for automatic prompt injection red teaming, which resulted in a more effective way to evaluate and defend against these risks. PIMiner is an agentic system that builds a strategy library to improve defenses. The research focuses on improving the security of large language models.

case_studies.title: From Score Matrices to Football-Aware Match-State Simulation: An Auditable LLM Harness for Exact-Score Reranking
case_studies.abstract: Football score forecasting combines a strong statistical core with a difficult contextual edge. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of accurately forecasting football scores by combining statistical models with large language models, building an auditable information harness, and resulting in improved score predictions. case_studies.title: DelusionEval: Measuring Delusion-Linked Behaviors in AI Chatbots

With growing public use of LLM-powered chatbots, there is an urgent need to build evaluations grounded in real-world episodes of psychological harm experienced by users. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of potential psychological harm from AI chatbots by developing DelusionEval, a protocol that tests a model's tendency to promote user delusions.
